newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-HOLDERS ENGLAND LOSE IN SEVENS QUARTERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HOLDERS ENGLAND LOSE IN SEVENS QUARTERS.

text.p: Holders England, with five full internationals in their side, were beaten 21-5 by a hard-tackling and speedy Western Samoa outfit in the quarter-finals of the World Cup Sevens on Sunday.
Coach Les Cusworth had warned that England had to break out of their normal 15-a-side style if they were to successfully defend the title and his forecast proved prophetic.

After a tight opening phase, Western Samoa scored through Terry Fanolua following a sweeping move from their own half, and a try from winger Brian Lima, who plays Super 12 rugby for the Auckland Blues, put them further ahead.
Afato Sooala made the score 21-0 with a converted try before England scrum-half Austin Healey put points on the scoreboard for the holders in the dying seconds.
The Samoans' dominance was underlined by the fact that England made it to the opposition's 22 metre area only on a couple of occasions.
"We did not have any direction -- we were still playing it the wrong way," said England fly-half Mike Catt. "We held our own early on but were not making any inroads. We never really threatened."
In the semi-finals the Western Samoans will play Fiji, who cantered into the semi-finals with a 56-0 win over tournament surprise packages South Korea.
Captain Waisale Serevi, who has vowed to take the Melrose Cup back to Fiji, scored two tries and eight conversions to bring his points tally for the event to 105 points.

South Africa made the last four with a 19-14 win over France but not before surviving a few anxious moments. Tries from Joost van der Westhuizen, Andre Snyman and Stephen Brink, two of them converted, gave South Africa a seemingly impregnable 19-0 lead.

But converted scores from Mickael Noel and Willy Taofifenua put France within touching distance. The South Africans will meet pre-tournament favourites New Zealand in the semis after they beat 1993 World Cup Sevens runners-up Australia 38-12.
Nineteen-year-old Calab Ralph of Bay of Plenty scored three tries to make winger David Campese's final game in an Australian shirt a losing one.
